title: 첫소리 ㅅ·ㅆ·ㅎ: 사다? 싸다? 하다?
objective: Tell apart and pronounce word-initial ㅅ, ㅆ and ㅎ, and choose the right word in pairs such as 사다/싸다 and 살/쌀.
summary: Learn three Korean first sounds that English speakers often mix up: soft ㅅ, tense ㅆ and ㅎ (h), with word pairs like 사다/ / 싸다 and 살/쌀.

task.title: CHOOSE THE RIGHT SOUND
task.line: Say each option out loud, listen for a soft breathy s (ㅅ), a tight s (ㅆ) or an h (ㅎ), then choose or write the one that fits.

words.exampleMeaning: I buy water at the convenience store.
I bought rice at the supermarket.
Are you free today? (literally: Do you have time today?)
What do you do on weekends?

letters.sound: A soft s with a little breath after it, like the s in 'sun' said gently. Before ㅣ it sounds close to 'sh' (시 ≈ 'shee').
A tight, strong s with no puff of breath after it. Tense your throat and say 's' sharply. Before ㅣ it sounds like a tight 'sh' (씨).

exercises: Fill in the blank with 사요 or 싸요: 이 사과는 아주 ____.
Fill in the blank with 사요 or 싸요: 저는 시장에서 사과를 ____.
Fill in the blank with 사요 or 해요: 저는 학교에서 공부를 ____.
Fill in the blank with 살 or 쌀: 저는 열 ____이에요.
Write the first consonant (ㅅ, ㅆ or ㅎ) of each word: 하나 / 씨 / 시간
